title: 3d Rougelike I'm vibe coding inspired by Zelda
author: ciddmandude
selftext: I've done this with asset store assets but the code is 100% vibe coded. Made with 3 weeks of a claude subscription so far. Not shown is that the levels are procedurely generated. Hope to have it finished in another month or so. This is only my second project with claude and I cant believe the results.

comments.author: IAmhowlshot
comments.body: This is awesome! You def captured a lot of Zelda qualities here. I see the vision

comments.author: AgenticGameDev
comments.body:
Great work! Looks promising. 
What engine? What workflows? What architecture? What is the biggest challenges in your mind?

replies.author: ciddmandude
replies.body: It’s unity. As far as workflow I wrote a spec and then had Claude rewrite it with milestones. I tell Claude to build a milestone and then test and tell it what to change. Biggest challenge is balanced difficulty with the enemy ai. My first version of the bat was unbeatable because he flies above you and spends very little time at your sword height. I eventually designed it to have a minimum distance from the player so that the swoop lined up better with the sword

comments.author: Eshinio
comments.body: Looks awesome, good progress for that short time. What LLM model are you using with Claude, and do you feel it's good at doing what you prompt for?

replies.author: ciddmandude
replies.body: I’m using sonnet mostly, I switch to opus when it gets something wrong twice in a row. It’s good because I’m efficient with tokens. I think the secret to vibe coding is having a good plan before any coding. Whenever my plan is wrong it takes much more tokens to implement. By that I mean I had Claude build something successfully but it wasn’t what I wanted. It’s sort of like building brick by brick and then suddenly you have to change the preexisting bricks. But changing the plan before a certain part has been implemented seems to work fine. So it’s more like you need a long term plan and then make edits for short term planning before coding
